executiveSummary: Indonesia: A powerful earthquake on Flores Island caused at least 68 deaths, over 200 injuries, and displaced more than 19,000 people; extensive damage includes 4,500+ homes and 370+ public facilities, with access impeded by blocked roads and landslides. Source View Article Colombia: A major earthquake in western Colombia severely damaged urban areas including Cali, with at least 287 deaths reported, nearly 4,000 injured, and hundreds missing as search-and-rescue operations continued. Source United States: Severe storms and flooding in Indiana and the mid-Atlantic caused multiple fatalities, mass evacuations, and disaster declarations; rescues and damage assessments are ongoing. Source View Article Canada: Wildfires in British Columbia's Okanagan region killed one person and forced more than 20,000 evacuations; large-scale emergency lodging and ongoing access restrictions point to protracted displacement needs. Source View Article Europe: A lethal wildfire in Greece (2 dead, 9 injured) and a large cross-border blaze in Belgium prompted evacuations and home losses, underscoring persistent regional fire risk under hot, dry conditions. Source Asia weather systems: Heavy rains in South Korea and the Philippines drove casualties, evacuations, and school disruptions, while Typhoon Dolphin triggered 300,000+ relocations in China and displacement in the Philippines. Source View Article Afghanistan: Flash floods in the east killed 23, injured 125, and damaged bridges, roads, water systems, a clinic, and markets-compounding WASH and access challenges. Supporting Report Figures vary across sources and are likely to change as assessments progress.

outlook72h: Indonesia (Flores): Expect continued access constraints from landslides and debris; prioritize road clearance and field medical support while monitoring for aftershocks. Source Colombia: Urban SAR likely to remain life-saving; anticipate shifting casualty figures as rubble removal progresses. Source US Midwest (Indiana): Risk of residual flooding and unsafe re-entry; continue evacuations assistance, debris management, and WASH support. Source BC and Spokane wildfires: Evacuation posture and sheltering likely to persist; monitor wind shifts and air quality; critical infrastructure protection ongoing. Source Source East/Southeast Asia: Continued flood/landslide disruptions possible where soils are saturated; sustain evacuation center support and WASH interventions. Source Source Forecast-dependent uncertainties remain; prioritize flexible logistics and protection for vulnerable groups.
